chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Bailing out the band in Texas after the Joe Louis fight week
summary: On the Linda Hopkins, James Brown and Little Willie John show, Cobb handled the master contract and had to send for money, and a hotel manager gave him a free week for playing a post-fight party.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, two years (inaudible) I told you I
took the Linda Hopkins situation out -- and during this time I was on crutches. With James Brown and Little Willie John and --
Oh, you were on crutches then?

On crutches, yeah. And Hal and handling the (inaudible) master contract on the show and paying off and doing the collecting and whatever, until I got to the jobs where we wasn't making any money at all, but we were running up hotel bills and had to eat. I had to call the office to send me some money to bail everybody out.

Tell you what happened, they had -- [Blackmon] and somebody had a championship fight there. Joe Louis was in town, and this was spur of the moment. All during this week Booker T. Washington, (inaudible), the manager, asked me could I get a group in there. We were going to have a party after the fight in his club downstairs. (Inaudible) gal that used to play piano with me, Boo Boo Pleasant.
Oh, yeah, she was in New York.

I'd gotten her and she got the rest of the rhythm section, and I took my horn and went down and played, and I just seeked money for them, and I didn't get nothing. But what the man told me, he said, "I tell you what I'll

do. I'll give you your rent free this week and your salary. (inaudible). Is that all right? So I stayed the whole week free. I went to the room after I got off. He had a bottle of liquor up there, bourbon, for my pleasure with a bowl of ice and a thank you note.
And I had to send to the office to bail everybody else out. Right.
